point: Parents give life; a true teacher gives the good life, which is one's relationship with oneself.
Βίος is driven by force and instinct; ζωή is warmed by fire and lit by νοῦς. Most people do not live, let alone live well.
Luck turns on fortune's wheel; eudaimonia is a stable fullness that holds whatever happens.
Paideia turns the soul's eye inward and cultivates virtue; schooling fills us with rote learning and technical skills.
Truth is a state of awakened consciousness; the cave is the realm of opinion, and no opinion as such can be true.
Information can come from anyone; knowledge must be conceived, gestated and born in you.
Pure eros is always beneficial; destructive things people call eros are attachment or obsession.
Physical tension is not yet eros, which is a cosmic current that changes you.
With Kazantzakis: in a relationship there are two, in eros there is one.
Fireworks lift morale but give birth to nothing; gratitude studies and practises the tradition.
Alone, without distraction, the repressed surfaces and conscience speaks; that is what we flee.
We live 'alone together' and mistake being connected for being with one another.
Only matter keeps its state; the more I identify with body and habit, the more inertia rules me.

b_gloss: you do not know who you are
point: The tax office and bills are not the cause; when you follow your deep heartbeat the chains have nowhere to sit.
Self-punishment is pathological; respecting shame means seeing the error, learning, adjusting and moving on.
Αἰδώς restrains us before a wrong; αἰσχύνη is felt after it. Its absence, ἀναίδεια, is shamelessness.
Shame is justice regulating itself in us; numbness is the real danger.
Doctors, teachers and therapists may be paid; what matters is pure intention and having walked the path yourself.

b_gloss: no one walks it for you
point: The journey is absolutely solitary and collective at once.
'Is not' means 'is not true', not 'does not exist': whatever rises and sets is μὴ ὄν.
From the One's view birth into the body is a death, and physical death is a return.
Philosophy practises the death of the persona, not the moment of physical transition.
Proclus: the soul descends by putting on foreign layers and ascends by taking them off until naked.
In gestation both happen at once.
The newborn lives the truth emotionally first and understands mentally only later.
First the One is sought beyond; then it is recognised remaining in everything. Both complete the cycle.

b_gloss: all is one, so I do everything
point: Two misreadings of 'all is one'; the ancients answered with virtue.
Opinions live in the cave, Ideas and νοῦς above; what awakens is beyond mind.

a_gloss: left and right, electricity and magnetism
point: Being has no opposite; within it there is only the possibility of forgetting.
In the Sun simile the visible sun gives reality; the Good's immaterial light is truth.
The sun and the Good shine by themselves; objects and knowable things are lit by them.
The sun of the Good gives light, the power to know, and heat, divine eros.

b_gloss: the incandescent lover of the Good
point: In every mystagogic tradition the knower is on fire with love.
A sensible παράδειγμα trains the soul's eye to navigate the invisible.
Where I want to find my rights I have probably lost justice, which is a collective balance.
Justice does not punish; it brings someone back to the Good and to virtue.
Wronging oneself radiates injustice; justice is a state, not a single deed.
We play a unique role and make an ethos, but we are the one playing, not the role.
The One is unknowable, so the aim is to merge with it, not to grasp it.

b_gloss: the mind not yet knowing itself
point: The outer cave is real but a reflection; the root cave is how we bind ourselves by thinking.
Stoic non-reactivity means not investing one's happiness in externals.
The universe is always in balance; we fixate on small local disturbances.
In Heraclitus nothing is created; the fire kindles and manifests.

a_gloss: to exist, stand under a principle
point: The One is, but does not exist, because it stands under no principle.
Part of the One stays unmanifest; part remains (μένω) as the monad and distributes itself without division.
Waves manifest but are never cut off from the sea.

b_gloss: the fiery nous that wears the soul
point: Knowing how the soul works is not yet self-knowledge.
Passions soak and stick; the soul warmed by the fire of the Good is wisest and best.
Physical flames are reflections in the cave of the primordial fire, which is Logos.
Poseidon's sea holds change; Diotima's sea of truth is fire.
The awakened see that the Logos is one and shared.
Her 'T' on the board: opposites live below, in becoming.
'Metaphysics' is a library label; for the Greeks all is φύσις.
The soul embraces the body; what is outside the body is the aura.
For the Greeks politics is human nature, not an agreement we may opt into.
Antiquity placed soul and consciousness at the centre; modern science placed the body.
Politics shifted from ideals, beliefs and religion to science as a means of power.
The lawgiver's laws habituate and initiate the soul.

b_gloss: a Taxisnet code and a vote every four years
point: Citizenship is sharing in judging and ruling, not a performative ritual.
By ancient criteria, some Greek thinkers say, we do not have democracy.
Democracy was born where people met to exchange ideas, not only goods.
Every experience happens inside the finite; awakening is a witnessing of the infinite.
Awakening is not knowing something new but recognising what you already are.
A vision keeps two; in Plotinus' witness seer and seen are one, so it is not even a vision.
The One is no-thing, not nothing at all: it is fullness without form.

a_gloss: God, Zeus, an angel, the light
point: As long as you see something you are not there yet; the One is no 'something'.
Following Plotinus, awakening removes what had wrapped itself around you; it adds nothing.
Energy, emotion or ecstasy may accompany awakening, but they are only its wake.

b_gloss: a product of time or method
point: Maturation is real, but awakening is ἀμήχανον, not produced by any 'machine'.
The awakened still play roles, even strict ones, without becoming them.
Once unity is seen you cannot work only for yourself; the ἰδιώτης was asleep in λήθη.
The Delphic 'κόσμιος γίνου' asks you to recognise your cosmic nature.

a: Einstein: God does not play dice
point: For Heraclitus the cosmic child does throw dice: the possibilities of the One.
As long as 'someone' is awakened, the separate self still stands; in truth only the Sun is left.
The One has neither inside nor outside and is both, so there is nowhere to go to find it.
She reads the Greek worldview as unitive, not as a flight from the world.
The philosopher's task in the Republic is purification, not rejection.
The return completes the path: the awakened raise the sensible to its highest beauty.
We are here not only to remember but to bring divine qualities from potential to actual.
The Same keeps us centred in being like Hestia; the Other carries senses, passions and changing moods.
Turbulence disturbs the revolutions, never the essence; so calm is revealed, not built.
The sense organs are doors; the mind is what senses.
Fullness does not come through the senses, but the senses can help as allies.
Conditions matter for cultivating eudaimonia but none of them gives the fullness we seek.
Seeking fullness in the next possession breeds endless wanting.
Through sensation a divine quality can pass from seed to flower.
Since the soul's essence is never disturbed, equanimity is uncovered rather than made.
Pure flower scents lift the soul; chemical and animal blends drag it down.
Philosophy as eros aims to become one with wisdom.
Knowledge activates an imprint already within, because soul and cosmos share one essence.
Knowledge must be left behind at some point, like a car at the foot of the mountain.
Paideia turns the soul from becoming toward Being and the Good brighter than Being.
Change the way of seeing and it leads to deification.
The Cave shows the difference; modern schooling about phenomena is not paideia.
If we claim to hold truth as 'something', we have lost it.
Separate in modern thought, one in the Greek tradition.
A mystery is unsayable, not prohibited.
Odysseus was always home; awakening is recognition, not travel.
If the puppeteer is within, there is no one outside to blame.
Luck turns with chance's wheel and passes; eudaimonia does not.
Nous is whoever perceives your thoughts; calculation is only a sub-function.
Earth is closer to the sun in winter yet colder: what matters is how you incline toward spirit.
Equinox brings balance and sowing; solstice brings maximum tension that can birth the inner hero.
Time is the moving image of eternity; eternity itself does not move except around itself.
It is the image that moves; eternity does not.
Excess flings you from the centre; a true school mirrors the Same in becoming.
Heroes symbolise the perfection of a circle of the soul.
To endure the path, rank love of Self, freedom and eudaimonia above every other desire.
Apollo asks consciousness to turn its eye on itself.
The elided inscription may allow 'know it': know the only thing that exists.
Her steadiness came with equal care for every form of life.
Plato: knowledge separated from justice is cunning, not wisdom.
Eros is the movement, agape the arrival.
For the ancients eros was not only bodily; bodily attraction is just the first rung.
We are collective first and individual second; the private man loses his human worth.
The Greeks add active help, like a mother's love, to mere abstention from harm.
The wise lawgiver studies nature and transcribes cosmic law into ethics.
She calls herself a lover of truth, not a knower, as the word philosophy implies.
The Golden Verses say if you leave the body, so liberation is a choice now, not an event after death.
The daimon is the droplet of God within, nothing like the later demon.
Reasoning plunges into number, so knowing abandons the unity of being.
Stopping at intellectual knowledge is a hindrance, not the fruit of philosophy.
Greek philosophy contains both.
The infinite has no contour to be experienced; we are it.
Hellenism holds both but leans to immanence, like Apollo shaking hands with Dionysus.
Hellenic ontology begins beyond consciousness.
Interchangeable in use, but she prefers Hellenic, as Greeks call themselves.
Plato regulated music and myths because sound and story shape the soul.
Hellenism is a way of seeing and living, not a slice of history.
Ethics is the habitual movement of consciousness, not a moral code.
Any thought, desire or emotion that blocks the soul's flow is non-virtue.
Two names for two movements of creative consciousness (her etymology).
Plato asked us to walk the path, not only to talk about it.
Religion tends to lose the spirit it organises.
Modern education trains the first and forgets the second.
A mob becomes a people only through shared paideia and shared beholding.
The universe is not irrational; matter itself has consciousness.
Comparative scholarship has value but is not philosophy.
Loving others nourishes my own soul: the pleasant joined to the beneficial.

a_gloss: relation to divine justice and cosmic law
point: Reading Homer theologically does not make it religious.
For Greeks the Odyssey is a symbol; for Hollywood it is raw material.
Ethics is knowing your psychic currents, not moralising.
Greeks visit their monuments as dead things, a sign of broken continuity.
Healing means going back to the origin to renew it.
Logos manifests through the mind but is not exhausted by it.
The first narrows attention on an object; the second spreads awareness until something is conceived.
Covid showed every external foundation can be lost.
Following Proclus, Athena's war removes what is monstrous so beings reunite at the intelligible level; Ares divides in the sublunar world. Wisdom always rules force.
Athena aims to return souls to the supralunar; Ares works in the dense, emotional, astral world below the moon.
When the One dreams the many it shows as Two forces, neither good nor bad; both are workers in the architecture of the cosmos.
Uncontrolled vital force becomes aggression; raised on purity it divides only to restore divine order.
What makes a law a law is the force that enforces it.

b: death as end of the dream
point: Death ends God's dream of incarnation and begins the return home; there is only transition.
The divine has both faces, and we must show each where it is needed, without guilt about strength.
The more refined we grow inside, the firmer we must be outside to protect it.

In her reading Greek statues stand and act: awakening must become action.
She separates the two: it was the religion, not Christ's teaching, that did strange things to Greek consciousness.
She marks θάρσος as different from both and promises to explain later.
The παιδεία of the cave is inner education toward awakening and eudaimonia.
Something in us was never bound, and it is what liberates.
You have all these, but you are the one aware of them.

a_gloss: in the world of the senses
b_gloss: the true state of what is
point: She says phenomena 'happen and don't happen': they occur on one level but are not fully true. This is her metaphysical view of events.
Searching for the exit outside only drives you deeper into the cave.
Not two places but two depths, or 'vibrations', of one world.
Each acceptance lets the Whole reveal its self to us.
The world itself, she holds, is a projection within the divine mind.
For the ancients philosophy's aim was to touch truth, not to master logic.
Touching truth shakes the whole being, not just the mind.
At the centre of existence each finds 'I am', and that Being is common to all.
The cave is the world of appearing; what is true does not change.
Plato adds a third category: the middle zone where the soul stirs and turns.
The real is the world of things; the true is the world of essence.
Mortals are gods who have died to the consciousness of the divine.
Socrates did not teach; he helped pregnant souls give birth.

a_gloss: pure consciousness without subject or object
point: Even essence has a source beyond it.
She reads the Pythagorean oath this way: Being flows, the Sun is its spring.
Identifying with the part is the soul's sleep.
The One is always present; we remove what covered us.
Death is not liberation; dropping the illusion that you are the body is.
You do not become a god; you realise what you always were.
Pythagoras united them in a Greek yoga.
Joined in Pythagoreanism, with no matter-spirit dualism.
Philosophy starts in the heart with the art of loving.
Ripened love makes the soul create 'as in heaven, so on earth'.
To make music is to tune the soul's numerical ratios.
Every mystagogical teaching has three levels, like a temple.
Logos is one and shared, though sleepers think they own a mind.
Pythagoreans held all-night vigils, so the symbol must mean the heart's fire.
We carry the seeds; we forgot them, we did not lose them.
The kithara is not its melody; the soul is not its desires, emotions or thoughts.
Observation lets us transform and replant our habits.
The two doors into the inner world; for many the pandemic was the touch of necessity.
Socrates speaks of turning the soul's eyes, not the body's.
Modern education neglected the soul's senses.

b: the pain of an unexamined life
point: Self-observation is hard, but a life unlit by knowing who you are is harder.
Eudaimonia needs both; thanksgiving activates grace.
The soul is the first polity; without self-mastery one cannot govern others.
Many Greeks are Hellenes only in potential; in 1940 they were Hellenes in actuality.
To be ancient is to stand toward the principles and the Good.

a: Hellenism as a seed in the DNA
point: Being Hellene is an existential, cultural and spiritual achievement.
Her claim: today's regime mirrors the tyranny of desire in souls.
Withdrawing into private interest is a cognitive state of forgetting.
You need nothing added; you only remove what covers the soul.
A reaction stays locked to the action it opposes; the «No» needs a «Yes» to bear fruit.
The hero touches eternity by dis-identifying from the ego.

a_gloss: fear, man innately bad, politics constructed
b_gloss: hope, man innately divine, politics natural
point: She grounds the polity in love rather than fear.
We love what we see as beautiful or good, even when others do not see it.
Hellenism is a universal spirit, not a claim of superiority.
Simplicity is the easiest road to truth; complexity can be a defence mechanism.
Awakening belongs to consciousness; an 'awakening of the soul' is only one stage, and the body is included only in the end.
Nothing changes in the world when we awaken; everything changes in us.

a_gloss: beholding, an inner shift of vision
point: Awakening is an often unnoticed shift of vision, not lights, beings or walking on water; nothing needs to happen because the One is already here.
Seekers confuse what happens around awakening with what it is; Apollo reminds us not to get lost in phenomena but to return to the essence.
Real knowledge of awakening is not the production of marvels.
Apollo takes no side; her coinage 'απολώσου' urges us to get un-polarised so the One can appear.
Apollo heals by simplifying: removing the many views and poles that complicate us.

a_gloss: a set of statements or rules
point: Propositions are true only by participating (μέθεξις) in truth, which is a state, not a list like the Ten Commandments.
Mantic knowledge comes directly in inner silence; at the first step we still go to a Pythia 'somewhere else'.

a_gloss: the popular image of the oracle
b_gloss: divine knowing of heart and nous
point: Mantic is not chewing laurel on a tripod but the sacred marriage of heart and nous; each of us is a seer.
She draws the contrast while explaining the archer's step, where the will stops changing and holds one aim.
Without opposition there is no harmony, so opposition is not to be feared but joined.
Delios manifests through signs and synchronicities; Phanaios shines directly. Plutarch names them together; splitting them is her reading.
At the last steps one stops living for one's own little circle and acts for the whole.
With Plutarch she reads them as two states of one universe, not rivals.
From 'I am here, the god is there' to living the god as a mode of the One; both views are true.

a_gloss: immortals, plural: first word of the Golden Verses
point: She notes the contrast while speaking of the shared 'we' of the last step: the mortal stands alone, the immortals are many.
Real meditation removes content rather than filling the mind with images.

b_gloss: lack of vigour, illness, inner στάσις
point: Living in the flow of eros gives health; illness is an inner civil war, in the psyche and in society alike.

a_gloss: heavenly: eros through spirit and pure emotion
point: Two qualities of the same power; societies promote one or the other.
'There is the individual and there is no individual': every act sends a wave through a shared ocean.
As we treat the one, we treat the other: sacredness toward oneself brings respect for others.
The same power cuts both ways: a double-edged knife.

b_gloss: keep away from eros, it burns
point: The Greek teachers ask us to know eros under a wisdom teaching with tools and criteria, not to avoid it.

a_gloss: all forces of the soul included
point: Leaving eros out excludes something of primary ontological importance.
Eros is to be steered by the divine nous, not by calculation.

a: diagnosing a polity by its arts
b: diagnosing a society by its eros
point: How citizens approach eros, from which energy centre and with what consciousness, reveals the society.
